subject: Next steps: Bluefield security intake — private deploy options & questionnaire
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lara O'Connell <lara.oconnell@bluefieldhealth.com>, security@bluefieldhealth.com
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: Bluefield security intake — private deploy options & questionnaire

Hi Lara / Bluefield Security team,

Thanks again for taking the time this morning — good discussion. Per our call I wanted to summarize the outstanding items and proposed next steps so we can scope the private deployment options (VPC-hosted vs on-prem/air-gapped) and begin the questionnaire. Key items we discussed:

- SOC 2 status and timing (you mentioned internal audit cadence)
- GDPR data residency needs (EU region preferred) and any specific retention windows
- HIPAA / BAA applicability for PHI in inference logs
- Network isolation approaches: customer-managed VPC with dedicated subnets, or fully air-gapped on-prem install
- Vendor security questionnaire kickoff (we'll exchange a completed copy)

What we'll provide this week:
- High-level private deployment topology options (VPC + dedicated subnets, VPC with transit gateway, on-prem air-gapped bundle). See attached checklist for the info we typically need to size the flow: redwood_private_deploy_checklist.pdf
- A short matrix comparing tradeoffs (latency, maintenance, evidence generation) and the documentation you'll need for SOC/GDPR/HIPAA reviews.

Questions for you to confirm:
1) Expected peak concurrent inference requests and average qps during business hours
2) Where logs/payloads must reside (EU-only or EU + backups in US?)
3) Any procurement timeline or milestones we should align to (PO date / pilot start)

Suggested next steps:
- You send back the Bluefield security questionnaire (or we can send our standard one) — either way we can do a pass-through and highlight gaps.
- Neha and I will prepare the topology diagram and a short note on air-gap feasibility by Fri 23-Mar.
- Quick follow-up call next week to review the diagram and the filled questionnaire (30 min).

If you can send answers to the three questions above and the questionnaire XLSX, we'll incorporate them into our proposal.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Lara O'Connell <lara.oconnell@bluefieldhealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@bluefieldhealth.com
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 13:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Next steps: Bluefield security intake — private deploy options & questionnaire

Thanks Stephanie — appreciate the succinct recap. A few quick answers and attachments from our side:

1) Peak concurrency: pilot expected ~50 concurrent sessions, production target ~800 concurrent sessions with spiky loads during business hours. Average qps ~120.
2) Data residency: EU-only mandatory for inference inputs and logs. We may allow aggregated telemetry to leave region but not raw inputs. Retention window: default 90 days, with a 7-year archive option for audit data (we would like options).
3) Timeline: procurement aims to finalize vendor selection by end of Q2; pilot start target mid-May.

SOC / compliance: We run SOC 2 Type II and have an internal program, but our external SOC 2 report is scheduled for Q4. HIPAA: Bluefield is a covered entity; we will need a BAA for PHI processing in production.

I've attached our vendor questionnaire (blank template) — bluefield_vendor_security_questionnaire.xlsx — and a partially completed section on data residency. Please pass this to your security teammate.

Can you confirm: do you support running with the workloads entirely inside our VPC (VPC peering / private endpoints), or does Redwood require the control plane to be reachable from your hosted control plane? We prefer an architecture where telemetry and model state do not transit the public internet.

Lara O'Connell
Head of IT Security
Bluefield Health
lara.oconnell@bluefieldhealth.com
+44 20 7946 0123

Attachment: bluefield_vendor_security_questionnaire.xlsx (xlsx stub)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lara O'Connell <lara.oconnell@bluefieldhealth.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: Bluefield security intake — private deploy options & questionnaire

Hi Lara — thanks for the quick answers and the questionnaire. Looping Rishi (runtime lead) for technical sizing notes.

Quick clarifications from our side:
- Redwood can run in a customer-managed VPC with private endpoints only (control plane access via an optional private link). We do not require model payloads to traverse the public internet; we can route control traffic over a private peering or private link.
- For fully air-gapped on-prem installs we provide an offline install bundle and appliance guide. Air-gapped setups are treated as custom engagements (longer lead time for packaging and evidence collection).
- For SOC/HIPAA evidence: we can provide architecture docs, encryption-at-rest and in-transit statements, and sample logs. The formal SOC 2 artifacts we provide depend on the deployment mode (hosted vs private vs on-prem).

Items we need from Bluefield to finalize a topology and estimate:
- Expected node sizes or compute constraints (e.g., allowed GPU instance families if on your cloud)
- VPC CIDR plan and whether you require dedicated subnets per availability zone
- Which subnets (private/public) may host the inference nodes; whether NAT/egress is allowed from those subnets

I'll attach a short visual summary of the network options we recommend for EU deployments (VPC private endpoints, transit gateway option, and air-gapped appliance workflow).

Proposed next steps:
1) Bluefield fills the questionnaire (we'll start a joint pass).
2) Bluefield shares a short environment brief (CIDR, allowed instance families / on-prem constraints, expected storage needs).
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with Rishi and network engineers (45 min) to validate the topology.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com
+1 (650) 555-0132

From: Lara O'Connell <lara.oconnell@bluefieldhealth.com>

Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 15:09:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Next steps: Bluefield security intake — private deploy options & questionnaire

Neha / Stephanie — thanks, that helps. A couple of follow-ups and the environment brief below:

Environment brief (pilot):
- Cloud: EU region on Hyperscale ACloud (eu-west-2)
- Allowed instance families: a2/g5 or equivalent for GPU (detailed SKUs to follow)
- VPC CIDR: 10.10.0.0/16 (we can allocate dedicated /20 per AZ)
- Subnets: private subnets only for inference nodes; NAT allowed for management host but not for inference hosts unless explicitly approved
- Storage: encrypted EBS with customer-managed keys; snapshot retention policy to be defined

Notes: we prefer the private endpoints approach (no public model traffic). For the pilot we can host logs in EU with a retention policy of 90 days.

I've attached a partially completed questionnaire with the compliance team inputs so far — bluefield_partial_questionnaire_filled.xlsx. We'll try to complete more of the security controls section before the technical deep-dive.

Can you propose two time slots next week (45 min) for the deep-dive with Rishi? Also please confirm whether a BAA template is available or if you prefer to start with our standard BAA language.

Lara

1) Neha and Rishi will review the partially completed questionnaire and add comments inline by EOD Monday (2028-03-26).
2) We'll prepare two topology options tailored to your CIDR / instance constraints: (A) VPC private endpoints + control plane private link, (B) On-prem style air-gapped appliance (custom engagement). Diagrams and tradeoff table will be uploaded to the shared Drive link by Monday.
3) Proposed deep-dive slots: Tue 2028-03-27 09:00-09:45 BST or Wed 2028-03-28 14:00-14:45 BST — please confirm which works best.
4) BAA: we have a standard BAA template; happy to start from your language if you prefer. I attached the HubSpot deal for reference so we can align procurement steps.

I'll also drop a short summary in HubSpot (deal BF-2028-014) and invite the Bluefield participants to the deep-dive.

Thanks — looking forward to the technical session.
